content.text: Hello! Welcome back. Today, we will build a stack ourselves using a simple C++ Array. This is the most common way to represent stacks in fixed-memory systems. Let's build it step-by-step!
We store stack elements in an array of fixed capacity. We use an integer variable `top` to keep track of the index of the uppermost element. When the stack is empty, `top` starts at `-1`.
Since arrays have a fixed size, we must manage two edge conditions:
· **Stack Overflow**: When we try to push a new element but the array is already full (`top == capacity - 1`).
· **Stack Underflow**: When we try to pop or peek an element but the stack is completely empty (`top == -1`).
